subject: Post-call: FinTechX concurrency qualification & quota path
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Porter <sam.porter@fintechx.com>, Procure Team <procure@fintechx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinTechX concurrency qualification & quota path

Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from call:
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 150ms for text generation at payload sizes up to ~512 tokens (chat use).
- Sustained throughput: ~200 RPS (steady-state).
- Peak/burst: up to ~1,200 RPS for short windows (5–15 minutes) during market open spikes.
- Concurrency: ~120 parallel requests at peak; we estimate ~60–80 long-lived streaming sessions concurrently during peaks.
- Streaming: ~60% of calls will be streaming (chunked responses), rest are request/response.
- Connection model: you would prefer connection pooling / multiplexing to avoid 1:1 socket per request; target ~8 logical request multiplexing per physical socket if possible.
- Security/region: US-East primary; SOC2 evidence will be required during procurement.

Attachments: I’ve added the SLO matrix we discussed (fintechx-slo-matrix.xlsx).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the steady-state vs. peak numbers above and whether peak length ever exceeds 15 minutes?
2) Who is the procurement contact we should draft an initial Commercial Reservation/Ratecard for?
3) Are you open to a hybrid approach (reserved baseline + burst credit pool) that lets you keep costs predictable while allowing short-term spikes?

I’ll loop Laura (solutions) and Ben (pricing) to propose a concrete reservation + burst design and a sample quote once you confirm the numbers.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: fintechx-slo-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sam Porter <sam.porter@fintechx.com>

Cc: Procure Team <procure@fintechx.com>, ops@fintechx.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinTechX concurrency qualification & quota path

Dev — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding extra detail: 

- Steady state is 180–220 RPS (we saw inbound at 210 RPS last week).
- Peak can spike to ~1,200 RPS but typically only ~8–12 minutes; during some scheduled events (earnings) we may see ~25 minutes.
- Concurrency: 120 parallel at peak is accurate. Of those, roughly 60% will be streaming (server-sent chunks for progressive card rendering). Streams are typically 2–7 seconds.
- Connection pooling is a must — we want to avoid opening >200 sockets from our service. If you can support 6–10 multiplexing per connection that helps a lot.
- Region: US-East primary, US-West DR.

Procurement contact: procure@fintechx.com (Procure Team). They’ll need a line-item quote, expected SLA, and SOC2 cert PDF.

We’ve attached our internal traffic profile for the last 30 days (internal only) — I’ll share with you via the Google Drive link shortly.

Sam
Sam Porter
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechX
sam.porter@fintechx.com | +1 (212) 555-0246

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinTechX concurrency qualification & quota path — proposed approach

Sam — appreciate the details. Based on your profile, here’s a pragmatic two-tier recommendation we can quote and pilot quickly: 

1) Reserved baseline (monthly committed):
   - Provision for 200 RPS sustained with a guaranteed connection pool sized to maintain ~80 concurrent long-lived sessions.
   - Target latency SLO: 95p <= 150ms on 512-token workloads (we’ll include perf runbook).

2) Burst / credit pool (temporary tolerance for spikes):
   - Elastic burst allowance up to 1,200 RPS for short windows. Burst is consumed from a shared credit pool; automatic throttling policy triggers at 90% of reservation and falls back to a lighter model variant if concurrency exceeds safety.
   - Suggested burst window handling: allow 15-minute undamped bursts with configurable soft/ hard caps.

Connection / streaming optimizations:
- Encourage long-lived keep-alive sockets with multiplexing (we support up to 12 logical streams per connection in our Dedicated offering; parameterizable).
- For streaming sessions: use chunked transfer with small initial prefix caching to mitigate cold-KV fetches.
- KV/prefix caching: we can keep session context hot for active users to reduce repeated encoder work.

Pricing & documentation: I’ve attached the current ratecard (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) and a draft SLO amendment that maps the above to a 12-month Dedicated commitment. If you prefer a shorter pilot, we can do a 3-month trial with a lower reservation and higher burst rates.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev/Ben: prepare a sample line-item quote for the 12-month reserved + burst model.
- Sam: confirm whether Procurement prefers a single DocuSign for commitment + SOW or separate PO flow.
- Once we agree, we’ll generate a HubSpot deal and a DocuSign quote; Ben will include the cost buckets and expected monthly spend.

I’ll also include a short runbook for connection tuning (keepalive, max-concurrency/per-connection knobs) so your infra team can configure their client stack.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com | +1 (617) 555-0299

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf, proposal-slo-amendment.docx
